newsitem.title: CHILE: China keen to invest in Chile's copper industry.
newsitem.headline: China keen to invest in Chile's copper industry.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng met Chilean officials on Thursday on the second day of a visit to seek a deal with Chile's copper producers to fuel China's booming copper industry.

"China's priority is to invest in the copper industry, which could include buying a mine," said Alex Fuentealba, of the Asian and Oceania affairs department at the government export promotion agency ProChile. "There is great interest that is going to materialise in the short term."
Chile is the world's largest copper producer, with over a third of global output.
The state copper corporation Codelco held talks with Chinese officials to discuss ways of boosting co-operation, including investment in mining and the sale of technology.

Li, who is on a three-nation Latin American tour, is the latest Asian leader to visit a region whose economic stability has made it attractive to Asian businessmen keen to exploit its mineral, forestry and oil resources.
His trip follows visits this year by Japanese leader Ryutaro Hashimoto and South Korean premier Kim Young-sam.

Li is the first Chinese premier to visit Chile and trade has dominated his agenda, brushing aside questions on international criticism of China's human rights record at a news conference on Wednesday.

Although Chilean President Eduardo Frei, who met Li on Wednesday, has given enthusiastic backing to China's interest in the copper industry, China may find it difficult to fulfil its aim of buying a large mine outright.
"The problem is no one wants to sell a big mine so the Chinese may have to compromise and buy a smaller pit which they could expand later," said one metals trader.
He estimated China will need 1.4 million tonnes of copper next year with its own production coming to 800,000 tonnes.
Chile is also looking to the Asian powerhouse as a huge new market for a range of its products, including forestry, fresh fruit and meat exports.
Chile was recently declared free of foot-and-mouth disease and erradicated the Mediterranean fruit fly, clearing the way for millions of dollars of fruit and beef exports to Asia.
Chilean firms are also interested in setting up factories there to take advantage of cheap labour costs, said Fuentealba.
Li visits Brazil next and continues to Venezuela next week.
